messages:
Alex: Quick thread — I re-ran RICE for the Q2 slate and the scores for adaptive-routing vs. batching/caching optimizations flipped depending on the confidence input. Need quick sync on assumptions before we lock the quarter.
Priya: Which assumptions changed? reach or confidence?
Alex: Mostly confidence. We got new telemetry showing lower error rates on routing fallbacks, so I bumped confidence for adaptive-routing. But batching has a stronger cost delta per-token.
Sam: From eng-cost POV batching yields ~18% unit cost drop on steady-state workloads. Impact is pretty clear for customers with high throughput.
Jon: But batching has infra risk — needs KV cache work and some runtime kernel changes. Estimate is 3 sprint of eng-runtime + 1 for canary.
Marta: Customer asks: two enterprise customers (FinCorp, Healthly) flagged routing consistency more than cost. They want predictable tail latency for SLAs. That pushes impact for adaptive-routing.
Grace: How are we modeling 'reach' here? Is it number of active customers impacted or percent of token volume? Our previous spreadsheet mixes both.
Alex: Good point — I'm using token volume. Maybe we should switch to customer-tier weighted reach (prod customers weighted higher). That would upweight adaptive-routing.
Priya: If we change reach metric mid-flight we'll need to re-score several items. Small ask: can we scope a lightweight canary for batching (no kernel change) to capture real-world gains before committing full work?
Sam: We can prototype a prefix-caching + microbatching canary that runs behind a feature flag in a week. No kernel touch. Would give us empirical per-token savings and latency tail.
Jon: That sounds safe. If the canary shows >12% cost drop with <10ms median latency hit, we can prioritize full batching. Otherwise adaptive-routing wins for SLA customers.
Alex: Proposed decision rule: run the canary for 2 weeks; if cost savings >=12% and 95p latency delta <=15ms -> promote batching. Else -> prioritize adaptive-routing for Q2. Agree? :thumbsup:
Marta: Agree on rule. Also add launch criteria for adaptive-routing: canary must demonstrate <5% error rate increase and SLOs maintained for 99.9% requests.
Grace: Who owns the scoring update? I can update the spreadsheet if you drop the new reach weights and the canary metrics.
Alex: Grace, please. I'll add the customer notes and decision rule. Priya, Sam, Jon — can you commit to the canary plan timeline in this thread?
Priya: I can coordinate customer comms and rollout plan.
Sam: I'll have the prototype ready in 5 working days.
Jon: Eng-runtime will allocate 2 engineers for 2 sprints post-proto depending on canary signals.
product-bot: Reminder — Sprint planning meeting at 10am Thursday to slot work items.
Alex: Thanks. I'll update RICE sheet with both variants, new reach weighting, and the decision rule. We'll reconvene after the canary window and finalize Q2 scope.
Priya: One more thing — let's capture rollback plan for both paths in the spec (timeouts, fallback-to-basic-routing, circuit breakers).
Alex: Good call. I'll add rollback/observability checklist to the spec doc and ping the oncall for a runbook.
Marta: Adding the two customer champions to the doc so we can validate acceptance criteria during canary.
Grace: Uploaded updated scoring here: https://go/repo/roadmap/q2-rice (link) — left comments on reach calc.
Alex: Perfect. Closing this thread for now, will post results when canary completes.
